column1: # SFA2 (arcade sfa2) ARRANGE trigger map: arcade command -> Saturn SFZ2 MUS song.
# Covers all 57 cues.  A map of only 0x01..0x13 would leave 40 of the pack's
# 59 arranged tracks unreachable -- two thirds of the arranged music unable
# Verified first: a service-mode sweep of 0x01-0xff on the real board (each
# command injected on an idle machine so it plays in isolation, clips cut at the
# true 59.637405 Hz) found 54 songs, and all 19 original rows were ear-confirmed
# to play the right tune. Only then was the map extended.
# The extension is mechanical, not guessed: sfz2_saturn_zero6_map.tsv already
# carries a duration-matched zero6_cmd for every song, and the pack's track order
# is track = saturn_song - 1 -- a rule that reproduces all 19 confirmed rows
# exactly (19/19). Four short jingles (0x16 0x18 0x19 0x1a) are included: they
# fall under the sustain bar but their arcade and arranged durations agree to
# Result: 57 commands mapped, 57 of 59 tracks reachable. Unmapped: arcade song
# 0x3e (no arranged counterpart) and tracks t19/t29 (S14 has no command in the
# manifest, S1E's command 0x34 is silent on the real board).
# Source of truth: manifests/sfz2_saturn_zero6_map.tsv (zero6_cmd column = arcade sound command,
#   validated via the A2-Gold zero6 comp2 dispatch table; sfz2-disc stage themes only).
# Join rule: cmd = zero6_cmd, song = saturn_song, for zero6_cmd in 0x01..0x13 (FAQ CPS2 order).
# Character labels (FAQ CPS2 order) mirror manifests/sfa2_snes_trigger_map.tsv.
# Consumed by build_pack.py saturn-mus --trigger-map (cols: cmd, song[hex]).
